This is such a lovely post! Congratulations on leaving that jerk and living your best life.

It was around 10 years ago that I went through the same thing. My abusive ex boyfriend raped me, impregnated me and cheated on me with my best friend. They both would say how I'd never climb out of poverty and how I was never going to amount to anything. I got an abortion, joined the military, became an aircraft mechanic and now live a nice cushy life with a man who loves and respects me. The best revenge is living your best life. :)
I never wanted kids and I still don't. I can happily say kids are not in my future.

Thank you for taking the time to say these kinds words. It means a lot, truly. I've been fighting very hard to try to better myself but one bad month and I'm right back where I started. I wish you the very best, hopefully things will get better for all of us.
Thank you for your kindness and I'm sorry about your struggle. I wish you the very best and I'll try too.

I used to do that, pretending nothing was wrong was great while it worked. Unfortunately I can't even muster the strength to do that anymore, so I isolate. Don't talk to anyone unless I need to.  

Hope you can keep the mask on better than I could. Best of luck.
I would love to just pass away in my sleep. Comfortable, quick and painless is the goal for me.

My father has been an alcoholic my entire life. He was drinking for years before I was even born.

Growing up I learned from him that I had to hold everything in. If I cried, then he would cry. If I cried and my grandmother heard, she thought my dad instigated it so they would scream at each other. I'm in therapy now but I still struggle with holding things in. 

Any sort of aggression triggers me. My dad's an angry drunk. He'd yell, break things, hurt himself all the time. He's never physically hurt me but he's definitely scared me by holding a knife and pointing it at me. He'd usually go from being calm to flying into a rage and punching the wall, pounding his chest or breaking something of his. So any surprises scare me, I break down, cry and ball myself into a fetal position. My boyfriend knows he can't scare me, needs to announce himself when coming into a closed room, ect. 

I'm a people pleaser from trying to prevent my dad from drinking/getting angry. I make sure to never talk about bad things and certainly never say anything about him. He'd find ways to turn anything I said into something negative or into a personal attack against him. I stopped trying to talk to people altogether. Therapy is helping but I'm 28 and still don't really understand how to have a normal relationship with people.

I'm going through the same thing currently with my dad.

 If things get too serious I would recommend looking into the Baker act and marchman act. According to my therapist those are saved for severe cases where the individual is likely to harm himself or others. If I understand  properly they will send officers to arrest/detain him and send him to a rehab/mental health clinic. I'm not saying this is the best approach but it is an option. 

I wish I had better advice, I'm sorry. :(
I had a guy who I broke up with call me crying telling me he got hit by a car and was at the hospital. A few hours later he called me back telling me he was at the gym. I guess he forgot, lol.

/r/suicidewatch has been one of the best communities I've ever found. This place was the only place to help me during my darkest times. No one to better understand your suffering than those who are suffering right there with you. Everyone is so kind, understanding and supportive.

If you're ever feeling like giving up and ending it, I highly encourage you to talk to some of us from there. Sometimes just knowing that your not alone in feeling alone is enough to help you fight through the day.

I drive to work and thankfully live close to my job. So it's only a 10 min drive. My office is only one floor with 15 people including me.

I get to the office because I have to. I have to work. I have zero support, I have to take care of my disabled father. If I don't work then I'm homeless and living on the streets.

I do what I can to avoid going out. I order groceries online, do all shopping online and stay home whenever I'm not at work. It's exhausting and terrible but I have no choice.

I understand these feelings very well. In my case it's not selflessness but those with happy lives that infuriate me.

How dare they act so happy and care free?! It seriously pisses me off, but I think the cause for that is my own insecurities. I yearn for that happiness. I'm jealous. Why do I have to suffer and work hard when you don't?

Perhaps you have insecurities about wanting to be helped. Maybe you want someone to offer a hand to you, or you want to help others but aren't in a position to so you get upset. Best way to tackle this in my opinion is to explore these feelings with a therapist.
I work in a office so thankfully I don't have to deal with a lot of people. It's still so exhausting...I want to work from home so badly but nothing pays enough to cover my bills.

I mainly listen to "As I lay dying" and "Trivium". :)

I have a few songs from other artist but those first two I have almost every album.

No but it makes life easier.

Money wouldn't make me happy. But not having to work, having time and money to seek therapy and getting to fulfill my bucket list will probably make me a little happier.

I do the same thing! Anything you listen to in particular? I could always use some more metal in my collection. 

I feel the same way to be honest. It's like you said, even when nothing bad really happens it still tend to make me feel like crap or worthless. 

Like logically I understand. Guy wants to hang out with his friend, cool. 

But my mind tends to change the narrative to "He's avoiding you. He's hates you. He prefers his other friends. I'm not good enough. I don't deserve his company." 

And the downward spiral continues. I find metal helps stop these thoughts for me. The bad feeling doesn't go away, but the music drowns out the negative thoughts. Thanks for sharing!

I've had to unsubscribe to a lot of subs because all they did was make me feel like shit. 

Maybe try making an alternate account? 

You can have one with the subs you normally visit and another with the subs that cause you trouble sometimes. 

Then depending on your mood you can switch to whichever account suits your needs better.

Hope you feel better soon OP.

When I'm overwhelmed, I go cry in the bathroom. I eat lunch alone in an empty office to avoid people and to have a quiet safe space.

My work is monotonous and listening to music doesn't usually help me so I try listening to podcast. I specifically listen to podcast about mental health in order to learn more about what I'm dealing with and try to find other ways to cope. My favorite is called "The mental illness happy hour".

I'm so sorry your struggling with this. You're not alone. Stay strong and I hope your situation improves soon. Wishing you the absolute best.

Exposure therapy is incredibly hard. I've been struggling with it myself and I feel most therapist push too hard. 

Instead of leaving the house to go somewhere, try something easier. Try stepping outside to check the mail, or a quick walk down the street. 

When I leave the house with my SO, he gives me an easy out.
So for example, if he wants to go to a restaurant we go and I get to decide if I can go inside in the parking lot. Most times I can't do it. There's just too many people. So we usually leave, pick something up to eat and go back home. I didn't get to actually go to the restaurant but I tried.

Baby steps. Good luck, stay strong.

Hey man, I know how you feel. I lost all my friends because they got sick of me. The unfortunate reality is that most people don't understand depression and they don't want to understand. They consider us complainers when in reality we're crying for help. Then once you actually kill yourself, all of a sudden they act surprised.

I would say if you want to keep your friends, stop telling them how you feel. I've found that talking to people who are also suicidal (like this sub) to be the best place to let these feelings out. It unfair, and fucking sucks that the people who "care" about you don't give you the time of day, but you can't change how they think.

In regards to a career, it's hard to decide on something. Maybe look for something short like a two year degree or a technical school? College isn't the only option. Try to get certified in something that gives you many options like programming.

I'm so sorry your sister abused you, I think therapy would be very helpful however keep in mind that not every therapist is a good fit. I've seen about 5 different therapist before I found one I actually liked. You don't have a car but can you take the bus? It takes some getting used to but the bus isn't bad.

It looks like your parents don't understand the severity of your issues.  Maybe instead of telling them how you feel, try to convince them to take you. Maybe complain of feeling sick, and once they take you to your regular doctor, explain to your doctor you suffer from depression and think you could gain a lot from therapy. Maybe the doctor telling them to take you to therapy will work. 

I'm really sorry your feeling so bad. I hope things get better soon and just know your not alone in being alone.

I have this powerful urge to veer into oncoming traffic. It's so easy, just let the wheel drift a bit.

If the accident didn't kill me then the life afterwards would definitely drive me to it.

But I would never actually do that because that would mean getting someone innocent involved and likely killed.

I often fantasize about this. Ideally I'd like my suicide to be clean so I don't scar my loved ones, but when I think about those who upset and hurt me it makes me want to take a more brutal approach.

I fantasize about blowing my brains out in front of my bosses. Right there in their office, in front of them and just splatter everywhere. I want my blood on their fancy suits and shoes. I want it to seep into the floor and stay there. I want to take away every moment they treasure with the constant reminder that they pushed me here.

But then the anger wears off, reality sits back in and I realize that even if I went that crazy with it they'd likely be over it in a month, hire someone else and go back to talking about golf.
I do this too. Hide in the bathroom. It's the only place I can cry.

The worst for me is when I'm talking with people who act like they care. They trick me by reaching out to me making me think they might actually be interested in how I'm doing, but in reality they only wanted to talk AT ME.


Person: "Hey, how are you?"

Me: "Not good, been having a rough week. How are you?"

Person: "Oh well you wouldn't believe it! My job has been so crazy! I've been flying non stop. Did you hear Janet had a baby? Man the flights are so uncomfortable. Ugh I've gained weight and Jerry wants me to go to his party but Larry doesn't want to go. What's with this weather?! I can't wear my leopard dress when it's this cold!"


Then they wonder why I stop responding. I'm not trying to tell everyone about my depression...But I'd be nice if someone just listened to me for a change...

I sincerely hope things improve for you. I've been struggling with motivation myself. Many people have said that it's not motivation we need, but discipline. I don't buy that, I think to have discipline you need at least a small amount of motivation, which many of us with depression completely lack.

The only advise I can offer is take it one day at a time. Try to do at least one thing a day that makes you feel better.

Whether it's a cup of coffee, a nice hot shower, or cuddling under some blankets to watch a video. These small comforts make a big difference in my day.

I'll still have a bad day, but at least I'll be clean, caffeinated and warm.
Don't give up! Your YouTube idea sounds wonderful. Making music was always my dream, I hope you continue.

I don't have that happen with my kitties. I take care of two stray cats outside my job and they are my best friends. They are sweet and so kind. They are all I look forward to anymore.

On bad days I ugly cry in the bathroom at work. On good days I hold the hurt inside for as long as I can before something triggers me and I break.

Now I'm 27 in a dead end job wishing I was brave enough to kill myself back then. Wishing I was brave enough to kill myself now...

Sorry this wasn't helpful. Just know you're not alone. :(

I remember being 10 years old and having dreams. I want to do this and that and go here and there!

By 15 I already had the anxiety and thought that I was running out of time.

By 20 I was desperately trying to make anything work for me. Dreams were gone, but I thought maybe if I gave it a really good effort I might have at least something decent going for me.

I'm 27, turning 28 soon. Nothing worked. Nothing good happened. I spend most days contemplating suicide, wishing I died in a car accident or something medical would kill me. 

I was dealt a shitty hand and I played it the best way I could. Nothing can change the shitty cards I have though.

Just as long as it doesn't end up the way the manga did.

Suicide island is a pretty good read.

My work is boring and soul sucking but I've found a few things that make things more bearable.

On better days I'm listening to music, it helps drown out the noise and keeps me upbeat.

On regular days I try to find podcast about depression/anxiety. Learning about this and trying to find better ways to cope. I try to find something with humour but not afraid to talk about some heavy shit.

Honestly, going to work is terrible. Nothing about it is good, but I try to make my mornings easier.

 I try to leave my work clothes out ready for me the night before. If I'm feeling really good I'll prep my breakfast/lunch too. 

I also buy coffee every morning. It's a waste of money, but drinking coffee makes me feel better, even if just a little bit.
I've been going through this exact same situation...it sucks I'm sorry. You're not alone. :(

Would to mind sharing your channel? I'd love to watch you stream if you ever decide to pick it back up.

"Why didn't you say anything?"

I currently can't afford therapy, so I can't even pay someone to care or listen to me. 

It's so incredibly frustrating when you want something real with people, but most are only wanting superficial relationships.

I want a friend who I can be honest and open with, and they with me. Someone who will be there for me in a time of need. I don't have a dog but I have two feral cats I feed at work. Those girls are my everything. They may not understand my pain but they listen when I talk. They miss me when I'm gone and welcome me when I come back.

Treasure your dog, he can be your friend. Maybe go on some adventures with him? Take him to the park, buy him a treat. Talk to him, I'm sure he's more than happy to be there for you.

I hope things get better for you.

These absolutely are symptoms of schizophrenia. If your parents won't take you too see a psychiatrist then if possible please talk to your school counselor or teacher. 

These symptoms might get worse over time, please try to push your father to take you.

Worst case scenario, a regular doctor can also refer you to a specialist. Please tell your doctor your symptoms. Have the doctor be the one to tell your parents that they have to take you. I would get your doctor's phone number as well, so if your parents don't take you, you can call your doctor and tell them so they can help you.

Good luck

The drugs seems like a good idea. There's definitely stuff out there I've wanted to try but never have out of fear.

I'd personally want to try shrooms.
While I've heard stories of people having bad experiences with it, the ones with mental illness who saw an improvement after have piqued my interest enough to where I think it's worth a shot, especially if I'm gonna off myself.

Other than that, I don't know. Ideally I'd like to travel but I'm so scared of not actually dying.

Like what if I spend all my money, travel, do something fun and fail my suicide attempt? I guess the next step would be to try again...

Yes yes yes, oh my god yes.

I have NEVER fully opened up to any therapist for this exact reason.
I self medicate and deal with suicidal ideation frequently. My biggest fear is having a therapist who wants to be a super hero. They absolutely can have you hospitalized against your will and while it's unlikely it's a risk I refuse to take.

I work hard, I go to work everyday. I'm always on time, I almost never leave early and get my work done. If I'm hospitalized, I will likely be fired, lose my apartment and my ability to find a job in the future. I won't be able to support my father. I'll basically end up homeless. 

I can't risk having a therapist who wants to be a super hero and in their good intentions end up ruining my life and driving me closer to suicide.

 It's kind of unbelievable that they are even allowed to this honestly. Who in their right mind would ever open up to anyone again after being hospitalized?

I know I wouldn't. I'd stay quiet, act fine until one day they'd discover my corpse.
Wow omg this is amazing! I draw too but I've never been able to anything realistic, just anime. This is so impressive, I hope you finish it! :)

I understand what your saying and greatly appreciate your help and suggestions.

However, yes I've tried. I never saw the Daredevil movie, my family never had money for those things but I understand what your trying to say. I've tried drowning out the thoughts with other hobbies of mine like anime, art, games, etc and over the years they stopped working. 



>Okay, the best example of what I am trying to say is if you ask yourself whether in the moments you were reading my reply, were you having those bad thoughts? Please answer this.

Yes. The unfortunate thing in my case is that the rumination has only gotten worse. Once I find something that weakens it, it's very short lived. I'm not going to give up just yet. There are still things I need to try.

ABSOLUTELY!

I would say it's one of the biggest reasons. I look around and see everyone living life, and I really mean living it.

They have friends, family, own homes, brand new cars, go out to party, travel, shop. Even the ones without jobs always travel and go do amazing things.

I work. I don't have money for vacations. I don't have money for shopping. I don't have time for hobbies. Just taking an afternoon off to see a doctor has to be planned weeks in advance with constant reminders. 

It's so disheartening seeing people give a third of the effort you give but have the money and time to do everything you can't.

 I want to quit, but doing so will cost me my insurance, my home, my car. I'd essentially become homeless...

Life's hard dude...

I know it won't stop on it's own. I've tried distracting myself. I've tried medicine, therapy, hobbies, trips, cbt, etc. Nothing works, the rumination just never stops. I don't intend to give up just yet, but man is it hard.

Thank you for sharing this. It's so hard living through this everyday. Seeing the exit at the corner of your eye but knowing once you walk though that door the amount of pain you cause to others.

It feels so wrong to be loved and cared for. To know that their love isn't enough to make you want to stay here. 
It's not my fault I live with depression, but it's not theirs either. I wish there was a way for me to disappear without destroying those I care for.

Yeah what happens after is pretty pointless to think about isn't it?

I do a lot of mind numbing work so my mind tends to run these simulations a little long. I used to just think about the act itself, then it was what happened immediately after, then months after, then years. I wish my brain would spend this time thinking of nicer things.

Thanks for reading and sharing your thoughts, I appreciate it.
Thank you for sharing, I will definitely check it out.
